gloss: to run; to dash; to gallop

definitions.gloss: to run; to dash; to sprint
definitions.explanation: To run swiftly, often with a sense of urgency or energy. More literary and vivid than {走|はし}る.

definitions.gloss: to gallop; to ride at speed
definitions.explanation: For a horse or mounted rider to move at full speed. Used in historical and equestrian contexts.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{公園|こうえん}を{駆|か}けている。
examples.english: Children are running around the park.

examples.japanese: {階段|かいだん}を{駆|か}け{上|あ}がった。
ニュースを{聞|き}いて、{彼|かれ}は{病院|びょういん}に{駆|か}けつけた。
examples.english: Upon hearing the news, he rushed to the hospital.

examples.japanese: {馬|うま}が{野原|のはら}を{駆|か}けている。
examples.english: A horse is galloping across the field.

examples.japanese: {武将|ぶしょう}は{馬|うま}を{駆|か}けて{戦場|せんじょう}に{向|む}かった。
examples.english: The general galloped toward the battlefield.

examples.japanese: {騎手|きしゅ}がサラブレッドを{駆|か}け、{観客|かんきゃく}の{前|まえ}を{一気|いっき}に{駆|か}け{抜|ぬ}けた。
examples.english: The jockey spurred the thoroughbred on, racing past the spectators in a flash.

notes:
An ichidan verb. More dynamic and literary than {走|はし}る (to run). Often appears in compound verbs.

COMMON COMPOUND VERBS:
- {駆|か}け{上|あ}がる (dash up)
- {駆|か}け{下|お}りる (dash down)
- {駆|か}けつける (rush to the scene)
- {駆|か}け{抜|ぬ}ける (dash through)
- {駆|か}け{回|まわ}る (run around)
- {駆|か}け{込|こ}む (rush into)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{走|はし}る is the standard neutral word for running. {駆|か}ける is more vivid and implies speed, urgency, or dynamic motion. {疾走|しっそう}する is even more formal and literary.
